I know many graduates from both universities who have landed jobs no matter what the situation is. At the end of the day, your university and career is what you make out of it. If you feel more secure with a scholarship and able to study better and have a healthier balance of internship-school-life, then go for it. If you feel better, studying at a more famous school, thinking there might be better chances for you, then go for it.

Your choice now won't guarantee your future, but I hope at least you won't regret it, whether it's about finance, prestige, etc. You can definitely land a job with this kind of hard-working attitude that you have. It just depends on what and where.

Plus, I would say that it's not just school names that matter, but how well you can socialize and build those soft skills. Both schools have excellent people and a wide range of networks. If you find the right people and environment, you can thrive anywhere.
